name: Ladder: Ping heartbeat
summary: PingMsg, wire 0x15d, type index 349. A 12-byte server-to-client record whose 8-byte body is a constant 2-byte prefix followed by a 48-bit big-endian nanosecond tick. The capture sends it first, before the self-identification record, and then about once a second for the rest of the session.
purpose: Keep the client's connection alive between and after the other rungs. The client answers every server ping with a 36-byte echo of the same 12 bytes, so an unanswered second of silence is what its state watchdog counts as a missing expected message.

created_when: the registration response has been answered
lifecycle.if_absent: the client's state watchdog counts ticks that carried no expected message and tears the connection down at the current state's budget

envelope: Record envelope (owned by javelin/frame.py, not a body field): the type marker followed by the prefix varint 9d 05 = 349 = 0x15d, so the 8-byte body below starts at record offset 0x04. The client's own 0x15d record is 36 bytes: an 8-byte head, a 16-byte zero run, then the same 8-byte body at offset 0x18.

fields.name: unresolved_prefix
fields.note: Measured 00 03 in the corpus record and in the eight 0x15d bodies a local session log carries, so it is constant. Its meaning is unnamed, so it is carried as a fixed 2-byte run rather than interpreted as an integer.
fields.provenance: legacy lab oracle: services/world/src/azoth_world/rep.py::heartbeat_body writes it as a literal

fields.name: tick_high
fields.note: The top 16 bits of the heartbeat tick. Read together with tick_low as ONE 48-bit big-endian nanosecond counter; the closed codec vocabulary has no 48-bit integer, so the measured 6 bytes are expressed as their high 16 and low 32 bits and the two fields are never meaningful apart. Measured 6ef6 in the corpus record.
fields.provenance: meanings.md '0x15d body: the tick is a big-endian nanosecond counter'

fields.name: tick_low
fields.note: The low 32 bits of the same 48-bit counter. Measured af912d74 in the corpus record, and the nine distinct captured bodies differ only here plus tick_high: consecutive pings are 1000000000 apart, which is one second in nanoseconds. The client only echoes the value, so the server continues its own series rather than matching the client's clock.
fields.provenance: meanings.md '0x15d body: the tick is a big-endian nanosecond counter'

evidence.ref: services/world/replay/messages-redacted.txt record 0x2_T0x15d_R.bin: 12 bytes, 8-byte body 00 03 6e f6 af 91 2d 74 after the 4-byte typed header, extracted by scripts/export/export-wire-bodies.py into research/fixtures/wire/wire-bodies.json and round-tripped byte-for-byte by the generated codec
the same dump's client answer 0x3_T0x15d_W.bin: a 36-byte client->server record carrying the identical 8-byte body at offset 0x18, so the client echoes the server's tick verbatim

eight further 0x15d bodies from a local session (research/fixtures/wire/wire-bodies.json, source log:rep_traffic.jsonl) have the same 8-byte shape and nine distinct tick values, all consistent with a 1000000000-per-second step
research/atlas/meanings.md 'The first typed exchange, measured': seq 0x02 is R 0x15d 12 bytes 'PingMsg', seq 0x03 is the client's W 0x15d 36 bytes, and both precede the 0x40a/0x1be/0x65c records

services/world/src/azoth_world/rep.py::heartbeat_body is the lab's oracle for the same 8 bytes (it writes the 00 03 literal and the 6-byte big-endian tick) and ::maybe_heartbeat sends it about once a second
